options: Marks a method as callable from Flow
Defines the URL path, relative to the org's REST base, that routes external requests to this class
Declares the class as a trigger handler
Enforces field-level security automatically on every method
questions.explain: The class-level @RestResource annotation defines the URL mapping that external REST callers use to reach this Apex class, relative to /services/apexrest/.

questions.q: Why must an Apex REST class and its annotated methods be declared `global` rather than `public`?
options: global and public are functionally identical in every context
Apex REST is meant to be called from outside the org, and global is the access modifier that makes a member visible across package/namespace boundaries
global is required only for classes with no methods
public methods cannot contain SOQL queries
questions.explain: global exposes a class or method across namespace/package boundaries, which is necessary for a REST service meant to be invoked by external callers.

questions.q: What happens to the inbound JSON body when an Apex REST method is declared WITH named parameters, like `doPost(String firstName, String lastName, String email)`?
options: Apex REST ignores the body entirely and the parameters stay null
Apex REST attempts to deserialize the JSON body directly into the named parameters, matching JSON keys to parameter names
The method throws a compile error, since REST methods can't have parameters
The raw body bytes are always placed in RestRequest.requestBody regardless of parameters
questions.explain: When a REST method has parameters, Apex REST attempts to deserialize the incoming JSON directly into those parameters; only a parameterless method receives the raw body on RestRequest.requestBody.

questions.q: What does `RestContext.response` let a method do?
options: Read the inbound request's URI and headers
Set the outbound HTTP status code, headers, and body for the response
Query the Case object directly
Permanently disable CRUD/FLS enforcement for the org
questions.explain: RestContext.response exposes the RestResponse object used to shape what gets sent back to the caller, such as setting the statusCode or adding a header.

questions.q: Which annotation maps an Apex REST method to handle an HTTP POST request?
options: @HttpGet
@RestResource
@HttpPost
@InvocableMethod
questions.explain: @HttpPost maps a method to handle incoming HTTP POST requests, parallel to @HttpGet, @HttpPut, @HttpDelete, and @HttpPatch for their respective verbs.
